dose.note: GSK's 7-day AMP-challenge crossover (1 and 3 mg once daily, 2005-06) set the regimen later carried into the 28-day trial.
dose.short: AMP challenge set a 1 mg once-daily regimen
dose.quote: Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, 3-way Crossover Study to Investigate the Effect of 7-days Repeat Once Daily Inhaled Doses of GW870086X Administered Via DISKHALER on Airway Responsiveness to AMP in Mild Steroid-naive Male Asthmatics
dose.confidence_note: Registry record (tier 3) used as the proxy opener, as the draft does for this NCT; dosing actually began 2005-10-07 (CT.gov actual start) and the record was first posted 2007-06-07. No results were ever posted; the result appeared only as Leaker 2015.
dose.judgement: GSK ran GW870086X 1 and 3 mg once daily for 7 days against placebo in a 20-subject (17 completers) three-way crossover reading PC20 AMP, FeNO, urinary cortisol and osteocalcin (SIG102335, 2005-06). AMP bronchoprovocation is a different human system from the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (different stimulus, mast-cell/AHR readout rather than late-phase eosinophilic response, steroid-naive subjects), so it is its own track per the track-identity rule; it was the earliest human model run for any member of this class. In dose it stated a regimen (1 mg once daily, effect to 12 h) and a tolerability margin (no cortisol or osteocalcin suppression), not an exposure target.

dose.note: The model's regimen (1 mg once daily, effect lasting 12 h, no cortisol suppression) was taken into the 28-day trial, reached, and failed on FEV1.

dose.quote: Estimated doubling dose differences for GW870086X 1 and 3 mg were similar across all time points, with mean doubling dose differences of 1.18 and 1.12 for 1 and 3 mg, respectively.
dose.confidence_note: The margin is qualitative (no cortisol or osteocalcin reduction at 1-3 mg over 7 days), not a NOAEL or MTD number. Whether the 2-4 mg adaptive trial (NCT01245426, unread) rescued the dose, which would make this 'target too low' rather than derived from efficacy, could not be verified within budget; dose is contra on either row.
dose.reason: Stated 1 mg dose reached, no FEV1 effect
dose.judgement: The challenge stated the dose and regimen (1 mg once daily, protection to 12 h, flat 1-3 mg dose-response read as U-shaped, Cmax similar at both doses) and that it was tolerated without cortisol or osteocalcin suppression. Patients were dosed to that regimen for 28 days without that toxicity and the FEV1 primary was null, so the dose row is 'reached, failed': contra derived from efficacy, counted once, with margin_stated true because the tolerability half held. No exposure or occupancy target was set, so the comparison is on regimen only.
dose.magnitude_basis: Regimen only; the model set no exposure or occupancy number.

efficacy.note: The challenge called 1 mg protective (PC20 AMP +1.18 doubling doses, FeNO down); the 1 mg 28-day crossover showed no FEV1 effect vs placebo.
efficacy.short: AMP protection at 1 mg; 28-day trial null
efficacy.quote: In conclusion, there was a significant protection against AMP challenge in subjects with asthma after single and multiple doses of GW870086X with a potential improved therapeutic index.
efficacy.confidence_note: Model side read in full (open-access letter, CC BY-NC-ND). Patient side is the Bareille 2013 J Asthma abstract quote already verified in the draft. The adaptive 2/3/4 mg dose-ranging trial (Bareille 2013 Curr Drug Ther 8(2):69-75, doi 10.2174/1574885511308020001; NCT01245426, 136 patients, day-28 FEV1 primary, no registry results) is Cloudflare-blocked and unread; Leaker cites it only for a 'U-shaped response'. If it showed FEV1 improvement at 2 mg, a later same on the row 'a higher dose later worked' would follow.
efficacy.reason: 1 mg protected AMP AHR; 28-day FEV1 null
efficacy.judgement: Prospective, not a retrodiction: the challenge ran 2005-06, before the 28-day efficacy trial (NCT00945932, 2009-10), and was published late (online 2015-03-14), so the comparison became public in 2015. The challenge itself tested the 1 mg dose GSK carried forward and called it protective with no dose-response to 3 mg; the 28-day 1 mg crossover primary (FEV1) was null, numerically below placebo. Unlike the mouse track, the model stated the dose, so the 'suboptimal dose' caveat does not rescue it: contra on the primary-endpoint rule. Comparison paired by the drafter: Leaker 2015 cites Bareille's adaptive trial for a U-shaped response but never sets the challenge beside the failed FEV1 primary.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: No common quantity: PC20 AMP doubling-dose shift (model) vs day-28 FEV1 (trial); the trial effect was null, not scaled.

considered_not_added: SUN-597 / S-0597 / SPARC-1316 (NCT02041221, Sun Pharma Advanced Research Co., phase 1/2 SAD/MAD in healthy men and asthmatics, first posted 2014-01-20, results posted 2016-03-31, primary = adverse events; HRA-registered allergen-challenge PoC in mild asthma): a third member on the existing allergen-challenge-lar track, uncompared (no SUN-597 efficacy trial), so it belongs to that track, not a new system.

Healthy-volunteer cortisol/osteocalcin PD (Werkstrom 2016 doi 10.1111/bcpt.12621, epub 2016-07-08, AZD5423; Prothon 2022 doi 10.2147/DDDT.S334960, epub 2022-02-23, velsecorat): the human counterpart of the rat thymic-involution readout on the existing rat-allergic-lung-oedema-az track (engagement, subjects healthy_volunteers, readout_tier downstream), not a new model system.

Kuna 2017 AZD5423 in COPD (doi 10.1111/bcpt.12768, PMID 28212463, 'did suppress 24-hr cortisol'): an imported safety comparison (imported_from MONDO:0005002) for the existing rat track, not a new system.

Pinkerton et al., ATS 2021 A1418 'Velsecorat (AZD7594), a SGRM Demonstrates Favorable Pre-Clinical Efficacy vs Safety Profile Compared to ... Fluticasone Furoate' (doi 10.1164/ajrccm-conference.2021.203.1_meetingabstracts.a1418, Crossref published-online 2021-05-03): abstract text unobtainable (atsjournals 301s to the OUP home page; Crossref and Semantic Scholar carry no abstract; Imperial citation page empty), so the model system cannot be identified or given a model_id. Prothon 2022 cites only the Sephadex rat lung-oedema model (Hemmerling 2017, the existing rat track). Remains a retrodiction candidate (published after the 2b posted 2020-11-27); retro vs contra undecidable unread.

Bareille 2013 Curr Drug Ther 8(3) allergen-challenge report (doi 10.2174/15748855113089990005): tier-1 record of the existing allergen-challenge-lar track; a dating/tier correction for efficacy entry 8, not a new system.

Boger 2016 mechanistic airway deposition/dissolution/absorption model of AZD5423 exposure (doi 10.1089/jamp.2016.1306, PMID 27740878; 'simulated systemic exposure well predicted observed systemic exposures' in healthy volunteers across two nebulisers and two DPIs): an in-silico PK model fitted against the clinical data for device bridging, setting no dose, exposure or efficacy target, so no cell it bears on; also effectively a retro-fit.

Isolated perfused rat lung ex-vivo absorption model (doi 10.1208/s12248-020-00456-x) and ex-vivo rat lung dissolution model (doi 10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.9b00289): rat-to-rat PK predictions for AZ inhaled compounds, no patient comparison.
Mixed-effects hidden Markov model of home PEF in the velsecorat 2b (doi 10.1002/psp4.70281, 2026): a retrospective analysis method applied to GRANIT data, not a predictive model.

In-vitro GR assays (A549/BEAS-2B/16HBE transrepression vs transactivation, trabecular-meshwork cells, 16HBE tight junctions; Uings 2013 and the 2020 systematic review): mechanistic premise of the dissociated-steroid class, not a disease model with a patient comparison; the draft already says so.
Chupp et al., ATS 2021 A1202 (GRANIT): a trial report, not a model; nothing to add.

Not a model but a finding for the existing tracks: the draft's claims that NCT01245426 'was never reported' (dose entry 4) and that 'GSK ran no further asthma efficacy trial' (efficacy entry 5) are wrong. The adaptive 2/3/4 mg dose-ranging trial (136 persistent asthmatics, day-28 FEV1 primary, Dec 2010-Jul 2011) was published as Bareille et al., Curr Drug Ther 2013;8(2):69-75, doi 10.2174/1574885511308020001 (Crossref issued 2013-09-01), cited by Leaker 2015 (ref 7) for a 'U-shaped response' and summarised by the 2020 systematic review as 'improved lung function'. Text unread (Bentham/Ingenta Cloudflare-blocked); if it shows a positive FEV1 primary at 2 mg, the mouse, allergen and AMP tracks each gain a later same on the 'higher dose later worked' row.
